about.title: About Medi
about.intro_p1: Medi is a medical wallet application that lets you store and organize your medical records in one place. You can search for a doctor of your choosing and allow them to view your records and summaries (if you generate them first). You choose which medical records and summaries to show or hide from each doctor, no information is shared without your consent.
about.intro_p2: From your records, you can generate medical summaries, either SOAP note, Medical Report, or Referral Letter to bring to doctor appointments. This gives doctors the context they need to make more informed decisions when there is no time to go through the details of all the medical records individually.
about.intro_p3: Medi is built around four user types: independent users, guardians, dependent users operating under a guardian, and doctors. A single account can cover all four. You can switch between them from the Profile tab, under the Account section.
about.ddl_indep_p1: An independent account is for users who manage their own records.
about.ddl_indep_p2: You can upload your medical records and include the reason behind getting the medical test done, the chief complaint, so your records carry the context that makes them useful.
about.ddl_indep_p3: Medi supports three types of medical summaries that you can generate from your records and share with doctors during appointments for a more complete picture.
about.ddl_indep_p4: If something in your records is unclear, you can ask Medi AI to explain it. Please note that Medi AI doesn't diagnose, it's there to help you make sense of what you're reading. Because it has access to your records, its answers are tailored to your situation rather than being generic.
about.ddl_indep_p5: You can grant a doctor access to your uploaded records and/or summaries.
about.ddl_guardian_p1: A guardian account is for those managing someone else's medical records.
about.ddl_guardian_p2: For each dependent, you can upload their medical records and include the reason behind each test or visit, the chief complaint, so the records carry the context that makes them useful. Records, summaries, Medi AI chats, and doctor access are all kept completely separate for each dependent you manage.
about.ddl_guardian_p3: Medi supports three types of medical summaries that you can generate from a dependent's records and share with their doctors during appointments for a more complete picture. The three summaries are SOAP note, medical report, and referral letter.
about.ddl_guardian_p4: If something in a dependent's records is unclear, you can ask Medi AI to explain it. Please note that Medi AI doesn't diagnose, it's there to help you make sense of what you're reading. Because it has access to the dependent's records, its answers are tailored to their specific situation rather than being generic.
about.ddl_guardian_p5: You can grant a doctor access to a dependent's uploaded records and/or summaries.
about.ddl_guardian_p6: If a phone number is added for a dependent, either during account setup or later from the Profile tab under Account, they can log into their own home page using that number and the guardian's password.
about.ddl_guardian_p7: Dependent users have a simplified experience. They can call their guardian, chat with a lighter version of Medi AI, and request access to view their records and summaries. When a guardian approves the request, access is granted for one hour. This limit is placed to protect the dependent's records from being accessed by anyone without their guardian's permission.
about.ddl_doctor_p1: Doctors can receive access requests from independent users who want to be added to their patient list, and from guardians requesting that a dependent be added.
about.ddl_doctor_p2: These requests come through the notification center, where they can be accepted or declined. Once accepted, the user is added to the patient list.
about.ddl_doctor_p3: From the patient list, a doctor can view the patient's records and summaries, depending on what the patient has chosen to share.
about.ddl_doctor_p4: Doctors can also remove a patient from their list at any time.
